memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then say to him, 'The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to say to you: Let my people go, so that they may worship me in the wilderness. But until now you have not listened. This is what the Lord says: By this you will know that I am the Lord: With the staff that is in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will be changed into blood.'" - Exodus 7:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before every plague, there is a warning. God does not strike without speaking first. Pharaoh knows exactly what is coming and exactly how to avoid it.

That tells us something essential about God's justice. He warns. He gives opportunity. Judgement in Scripture is never arbitrary or sudden for those who have been told.

Notice also the purpose stated again: let my people go, so that they may worship me. God's aim is not merely their comfort but their worship. Freedom is always freedom for something.

And notice the reason for the plague: by this you will know that I am the Lord. Even judgement is revelation. God is still, in a sense, introducing Himself to a man who asked, who is the Lord?

The greatest warning God ever gave came wrapped in mercy — He so loved the world that He gave His Son, so that whoever believes should not perish (Jn 3:16). The warning and the rescue arrived together.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has God been warning me about something I keep postponing?
2. Am I using my freedom in Christ for worship, or only for comfort?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You warn before You act. Give me a heart that responds quickly to Your voice. Amen.
